key_insight: The paper characterizes when a nonconvex variable-projection spike deconvolution objective becomes locally well-behaved, linking convexity, identifiability, and convergence to point-spread-function properties and spike separation.
engineering_relevance: This provides practical guarantees for recovering sparse impulses from multiple noisy measurements, informing sensor design, bandwidth choice, and robust initialization for gradient-based reconstruction.
method: Eliminate spike amplitudes analytically via variable projection to optimize only locations.
Derive a basin-of-convexity characterization using PSF power spectral density, smoothness, bandwidth, and separation.
Use Beurling--Selberg extremal approximations to obtain sharp conditioning bounds and local convergence guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments that validate the theory and show modified ESPRIT initialization followed by gradient refinement works effectively.
watch_item: The guarantees are local, so performance still depends on getting an initialization inside the basin of convexity.
paper_title: Characterization of the basin of convexity for multi-snapshot spike deconvolution via variable projection
